رَازِمٌ A camel remaining fixed upon the ground, (S, TA,) unable to rise, (Lh, S, K, TA,) in consequence of his having fallen down by reason of fatigue and emaciation, (Lh, TA,) or in consequence of emaciation (S, K, TA) arising from hunger or disease: (TA:) and in like manner applied to a man, &c.: (Lh, TA:) and also, [without ة,] applied to a she-camel, meaning standing still, or stopping from journeying, in consequence of fatigue and emaciation, and motionless: (S:) pl. رَزْمَى and رِزَامٌ, [accord. to Freytag رُزَمٌ,] applied to camels. (TA.) ―
-b2- See also مَرْزِمٌ. ―
-b3- Also, applied to winter, Cold. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
